name: Perihelion Gait-Tuned Running Shoe
description:
Perihelion builds each shoe around a full biomechanical analysis of the buyer's running gait — appointments include treadmill scanning, joint load mapping, and a BCI session to capture neuromuscular firing patterns. The resulting shoe has a custom midsole geometry, a carbon fiber propulsion plate tuned to the wearer's stride, and an upper knit to their exact foot volume. Performance at a level that corponation mass-market shoes can't touch.

Worn by serious Tier 4-5 athletes who compete in amateur circuits, executives who treat their morning run as a competitive event, and anyone who can justify the price as an investment in their body.
functionality: Gait-optimized propulsion. Reduces injury risk through custom joint load distribution. BCI-linked real-time performance feedback optional.
what_it_says: You take your body as seriously as your career. You had your gait analyzed and you paid someone to fix it.
story_hooks: Perihelion's gait database was subpoenaed in a murder case — the biomechanical profile of the suspect's stride matches security footage perfectly.
A Perihelion shoe built for someone with a specific leg augmentation has been ordered under a false name. The biomechanical specs don't match any registered aug configuration.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, anatomically aggressive running shoe with an elevated heel-toe differential and a pronounced carbon fiber shank visible through translucent side panels. The upper wraps the foot like a second skin, with minimal excess material. The silhouette is forward-leaning, almost predatory—built for velocity, not leisure.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight through the midfoot and heel, with a snug but not restrictive forefoot box. The collar sits low and ergonomic. Zero dead space; every curve matches individual biomechanics. Feels like an extension of the leg rather than something worn on it.
physical_description.primary_material: Performance knit upper (likely recycled polyester blend with elastane), thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) reinforcement straps, carbon fiber composite propulsion plate, expanded foam midsole with custom density zones, and sticky rubber outsole for grip.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost liquid-like knit with subtle ribbing at stress points. The carbon fiber plate creates a subtle ridge visible through semi-translucent side panels. Outsole is tactile and grippy, worn matte rather than glossy.
physical_description.color_scheme: Monochromatic performance colorway—deep charcoal or gunmetal base with accent hits of electric cyan or neon violet along the Perihelion logo and propulsion plate edge. Possibly iridescent threading in the knit that shifts under light.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snap toggle at the heel collar for quick on-off, paired with a friction-fit upper that locks the foot in place. No traditional laces—the knit itself provides dynamic compression.
distinctive_features: Transparent TPU side panel revealing the carbon fiber propulsion plate geometry
Perihelion logo embossed (not printed) on the heel and tongue
Serial number engraved on the insole—proof of bespoke customization
BCI calibration mark (small hexagonal indent) on the inner heel
Micro-vents along the arch for thermal regulation during high-intensity runs
Wear pattern: pristine on delivery, but develops polished spots on the ball of the foot and heel within weeks of use
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 luxury with Tier 4-5 athlete overlap. The price point (likely 800–1200 Φ) signals disposable income or serious competitive investment. Not corpo casual—this is performance-obsessed.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by endurance athletes, neo-Olympiad circuit competitors, corpo executives who gamify their fitness, and sub-grade runners saving for months to unlock a custom pair as a status marker. Signals dedication to optimization, access to personalized tech, and a body treated as a finely-tuned instrument.
physical_description.condition_typical: Delivered pristine and custom-fitted. Within 2–3 weeks, develops a broken-in patina: scuffed heel, polished toe box, slight discoloration from sweat and weather. Rarely discarded—owners maintain and repair them for years, as replacement cost is prohibitive.
